stage6.name: Stage 6: Year-Weighted Constructor
stage6.description: Dirichlet-Multinomial with recency-weighted constructor priors. Best calibrated model (LL/race = -59.0). Trained 2015-2025.

stage9.name: Stage 9: Bayesian State-Space
stage9.description: Random walk on driver/constructor log-strengths with Plackett-Luce observations. Best top-3 accuracy (1.59/3). Trained 2015-2025.

composite.name: Composite (2-Model Blend)
composite.description: Equal-weight blend of Stage 6 + Stage 9 probabilities, renormalized.

agent_prediction.name: Agent Forecast (Claude)
agent_prediction.description: Predicted by Claude using web-searched current form, prior-season results, and qualitative judgment.
agent_prediction.rationale:
**Agent podium: Hamilton â€” Russell â€” Antonelli.**

The quantitative composite (Hamilton / Russell / Verstappen) anchors this call, and I keep its top two. Hamilton arrives on the back of his maiden Ferrari win at Barcelona, Ferrari has clear momentum, and the Red Bull Ring has historically been one of his stronger venues â€” the 31% composite win probability is well earned. Russell took pole and P2 at Barcelona; Mercedes has been the class of the 2026 field, and the Red Bull Ring's power-and-traction profile suits the car.

**The one place I override the model is the third step.** The models bury championship leader Kimi Antonelli at ~P10 (E[pos] 10.0). That is a seeding artifact, not a pace read: the Markov chain starts R8 from R7 finishing positions, and Antonelli's Barcelona retirement was a late engine failure while running second â€” a reliability event, not a performance one. He still leads the title by 41 points in the season's fastest car. I put him back on the podium ahead of Verstappen.

**Why Verstappen drops just off:** the Red Bull Ring is his fortress historically (four wins, home race) and the model rightly flags him, but Red Bull's 2026 form is genuinely midfield â€” he sits 7th in points on 55, and his Barcelona P4 was his ceiling rather than his average. I rate Norris and Piastri as the next-best podium threats alongside him.
context: Drivers' standings after R7 Barcelona: Antonelli 156, Hamilton 115, Russell 106, Leclerc 75, Norris 73, Piastri 58, Verstappen 55
Hamilton won Barcelona (R7) for his maiden Ferrari victory; first all-British podium (Hamilton/Russell/Norris) since 1968
Antonelli led much of Barcelona but retired ~3 laps from the end with a Mercedes engine failure while running 2nd â€” a reliability DNF, not a pace issue; title lead cut to 41 pts
Russell took pole at Barcelona and finished P2; Mercedes has been the strongest package across 2026
Red Bull Ring is a short power circuit (10 corners, big braking zones at T1/T3/T4, +65m elevation) that rewards engine/traction and produces frequent overtaking
Historically a Red Bull/Verstappen stronghold (Verstappen 4 wins) and strong for Mercedes in the modern era; McLaren has the most Austria wins all-time (7)
Red Bull's 2026 form is well off its usual level â€” Verstappen 7th in the standings, best recent finish P4 at Barcelona
No Austria-weekend data (practice/qualifying/weather) was used â€” forecast is based on form through R7 only
